title: Control plane rotations and ratcheting notes — 2026-07-19
content:
Attendees: Priya, Liam, Mei, Rohit, Ava (joined late), +2 observers from SRE
Meeting length: 40m (quick sync, followed by action triage)
Context / why this note exists:
- We ran a small experiment last week to ratchet Dedicated controlplane routing capacity in bursts (goal: verify graceful capacity increases without cross-region failover).
- This sync focused on operational feedback from oncall, a few regressions surfaced in auth handshake, and a proposal for a repeatable rotation playbook.

Agenda (rough):
1) Quick recap of ratcheting experiment results (Rohit)
2) Auth handshake delays and mitigation (Mei)
3) Rotation schedule + handover checklist cleanup (Priya)
4) Quotas oddities observed (Liam)
5) Action items and owners

Recap — ratcheting experiment (Rohit):
- Setup: 3 waves of capacity increase (+10%, +25%, +50%) over 36h on staging cluster with traffic replay.
- Observed: routing-controller successfully rebalanced pods; average route rebind time ~18s for +50% wave which is OK but peak tail was 112s when a node was draining.
- Unexpected: KV-cache warmup caused a transient p99 token-latency spike for models with long-context (>8k) while nodes imported cache shards.
- Cost signal: ephemeral burst adds ~12% GPU minutes during wave windows. Good trade for fast recovery, but needs limits.
- Conclusion: safe to adopt ratcheting as a default fallback for Dedicated, but must add guardrails for KV-cache warmup and auth handshake timeouts.

Auth handshake problem (Mei):
- Symptom: ~0.6% of requests in the +50% window failed an auth validation step when a new routing table applied concurrently. Failures were intermittent 401s with weird timing: token-validate call completed but session lookup returned empty because the auth cache invalidated prematurely.
- Root cause hypothesis: cache eviction policy (LRU) plus parallel routing updates cause short windows where auth middleware sees inconsistent session index.
- Temporary mitigation applied: increased auth cache TTL from 30s -> 90s for the experiment cluster; failure rate dropped to 0.03%.
- Long-term: remove coupled path between route updates and auth index invalidation; add an atomic swap pattern for session index pointers.
- Open question: how does this change affect memory pressure on smaller nodes? Mei to run mem-pressure matrix.

Rotation / handover playbook (Priya):
- Current pain: handovers are ad-hoc; partial context lost across shifts. Proposed lightweight checklist:
  * 10m pre-handoff: current alerts, active incidents, ongoing experiments, contacts
  * 5m handoff: one-sentence state per incident, hot routes to watch, recent deploys and PR ids
  * Post-handoff: update the rota doc with explicit owner + escalation path
- Proposed new doc name: "controlplane-handoff-cheatsheet" (Priya will draft).
- Rotation cadence proposal: keep 12/7 primary shifts; try a 10-day pilot of 24h oncall for small subteam (Rohit + Ava volunteering) — purpose: reduce context thrash.

Quotas and oddities (Liam):
- Edge case: multi-tenant bursts caused a quota fallback loop when a tenant hit soft limit and routing retried to alternate region — triggering cross-region rebinds and further quota signals.
- Action: implement a per-tenant backoff cap to prevent aggressive cross-region failover for quota-limited tenants. Liam to spin a spike.
- Data ask: need a visualization for quota-fallback loops (time series showing tenant->region attempts). Mei to add a dashboard tile on Console project.

Incidents / Bugs raised during experiment:
- BUG-1219: KV-cache warmup p99 spikes (Rohit)
- BUG-1224: Auth cache eviction race -> transient 401s (Mei)
- BUG-1227: Quota fallback loop for bursty tenants (Liam)
- Notes: Triage link: JIRA-PLTFM-4821 (contains raw traces and flamegraphs).

Decisions made during meeting:
- Ratcheting will be enabled as a canary fallback for Dedicated customers, gated by two conditions: (1) KV-cache warmup mitigation (see BUG-1219) and (2) auth atomic-swap patch deployed in canary (see BUG-1224).
- Increase auth cache TTL in canary clusters to 90s while we test; do not change prod TTL until patch lands.
- Introduce a short-lived per-tenant cross-region backoff to avoid cascading quota fallthroughs.

Action items (owner + due):
- Priya: Draft "controlplane-handoff-cheatsheet" and share in #pltfm-ops (due 2026-07-23).
- Rohit: Root-cause writeup for BUG-1219 + proposal for staged KV pre-warm on node attach (due 2026-07-22).
- Mei: Memory-pressure matrix for auth cache TTL changes + PR for atomic-swap session index (draft PR by 2026-07-24).
- Liam: Spike quota-backoff cap and add dashboard tile for quota-fallback loop (spike results by 2026-07-26).
- Ava: Run 24h oncall pilot plan doc and volunteer schedule (due 2026-07-21).
- All: Keep linked traces/observability links in JIRA-PLTFM-4821.

Notes to self (Priya):
- Need to revisit autoscaler logic: when we ratchet, pods come up faster than cache warms — maybe we should sequence warmup -> readiness rather than rely on steady-state cache propagation.
- Consider adding a synthetic traffic warmup job per node when joining cluster (small token set for top-10 models).
- Follow up with Console team on cost telemetry for burst windows — want per-customer cost delta.

Loose ideas / brainstorm (unassigned):
- "Graceful warmup" flow: attach node -> run scoped warmup of KV shards -> mark route-ready -> advertise. Could be feature-flagged.
- Soft-lease on auth session indexes: keep two live copies and flip pointer atomically (atomic-swap pattern mentioned in meeting).
- Quota backoff: exponential with jitter + per-tenant safety cap to avoid oscillation.

Meeting artifacts to browse:
- github PR: controlplane/pull/1378 (routing controller changes)
- JIRA: JIRA-PLTFM-4821 (experiment traces)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-CP-ROTATIONS-2026 (experiment runbook)

Next check-in: quick sync on 2026-07-22 to review Rohit + Mei spike results; full handoff doc review scheduled for 2026-07-23.

Unresolved questions (low priority):
- Will increased auth cache TTL cause unacceptable memory pressure on micro-instances? (Mei to measure)
- Does warmup job introduce exploitable traffic pattern that could be gamed by adversarial tenants? (security to advise)

-- end of notes --
